parts.latex:
An item was purchased for a price of \$880, including $10\%$ GST.

What is the amount of GST included in the price?

solutions.latex:
The price including GST is $110\%$ of the price before GST.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Price before GST} &= \dfrac{880}{1.1} \\ &= \$800 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{GST} &= 880 - 800 \\ &= \$80.00 \end{aligned}$$
This is option C.

parts.latex:
An item is discounted by $30\%$ and then a further discount of $20\%$ is applied to the reduced price.

What is the total percentage discount?

solutions.latex:
A $30\%$ discount leaves $70\%$ of the price, and a further $20\%$ discount leaves $80\%$ of that.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{final price} &= 0.7\times 0.8\times \text{original}\\ &= 0.56\times\text{original} \end{aligned}$$
The total discount is
$$100\% - 56\% = 44\%$$
This is option B.

parts.latex:
A receipt from a supermarket shows a total of \$124.87. The GST shown on the receipt is \$3.86.

GST, at a rate of $10\%$, is only charged on some items.

What was the value of the items which did NOT have GST charged?

solutions.latex:
GST is $10\%$ of the value $n$ of the items charged.
$$\begin{aligned}0.1\times n &= 3.86\\ n &= \$38.60\end{aligned}$$
The total includes the GST and the items charged.
$$\begin{aligned}\text{Items without GST} &= 124.87-38.60-3.86\\ &= \$82.41\end{aligned}$$
criteria: Calculates the difference between the total and the amount on which GST is charged, or equivalent merit
Calculates the amount on which GST is charged, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
A sports store sells jerseys priced at \$169.95, including 10% goods and services tax (GST).

What is the amount of GST included in the price?

solutions.latex:
The price includes GST, so it is $110\%$ of the pre-GST price. The GST is $\dfrac{10}{110} = \dfrac{1}{11}$ of the price paid.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{GST} &= \dfrac{169.95}{11} \\ &= \$15.45 \end{aligned}$$
This is option A.

meta.self_check: 169.95/11 = 15.45 in Python; pre-GST price 154.50, 10% of it 15.45.

parts.latex:
A bill for servicing a car is made up of:

\begin{itemize}
\item \$242 for parts, which includes $10\%$ GST
\item \$100 for labour, excluding GST.
\end{itemize}

The mechanic needs to add $10\%$ GST onto the labour charge.

How much GST does the customer pay in total?

solutions.latex:
The parts price includes $10\%$ GST, so it is $110\%$ of the price before GST. The GST on the parts is
$$\dfrac{10}{110}\times 242 = \$22$$
The GST added to the labour is
$$10\% \times 100 = \$10$$
The total GST is
$$22 + 10 = \$32.00$$
Hence the answer is C.

parts.latex: Explain the differences between compulsory third party (CTP) and non-compulsory third-party insurance.

solutions.latex:
Compulsory third party (CTP) is legally required and covers injury to other people in an accident.

Non-compulsory third-party insurance is optional and covers damage to other people's property in an accident.

Michelle wants to buy a 2-year-old all-wheel drive sedan priced at \$46 435. She has an offer of car insurance based on 5\% of the value of the car.

Michelle will need to pay stamp duty on the sale of the vehicle, with the rates being shown below.

\extable{720_q10_t1}

Calculate the amount that Michelle will pay to buy and insure her vehicle for one year.

solutions.latex:
Insurance is 5% of the car's value.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Insurance} &= 5\% \times 46435 \\ &\approx \$2321.75 \end{aligned}$$
The price is rounded up to $\$46\,500$ for the stamp duty table.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Stamp duty} &= 1350 + \dfrac{5}{100} \times (46500 - 45000) \\ &= \$1425 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Total cost} &= 46435 + 2321.75 + 1425 \\ &= \$50\,181.75 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct answers for insurance and stamp duty, or equivalent merit

parts.latex: Jacqueline buys a new lounge suite for her home. The GST inclusive price for the lounge suite is \$3200. Given that GST is calculated at $10\%$ of the purchase price, calculate the GST paid on the lounge suite, to the nearest dollar.

solutions.latex:
The GST inclusive price is $110\%$ of the pre-GST price.
$$\begin{aligned} \text{Pre-GST price} &= 3200 \div 1.1 \\ &= \$2909.09 \end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned} \text{GST} &= 3200 - 2909.09 \\ &\approx \$291 \end{aligned}$$
$$\therefore\ \text{GST paid} = \$291 \text{ (to the nearest dollar)}$$

An investment of \$50 000 increases in value by $9\%$ in the first year and decreases by $9\%$ in the second year of investment.

Calculate the percentage change, in the value of the investment, over the two-year period.

solutions.latex:
Value after two years:
$$50\,000\times 1.09\times 0.91=49\,595$$
Percentage change:
$$\dfrac{50\,000-49\,595}{50\,000}\times 100=0.81\%$$
This is a decrease of $0.81\%$.

parts.latex:
Jason wants to purchase a car for \$20 000 on terms with a $10\%$ deposit and $8\%$ p.a. flat rate interest, repayable monthly over 5 years.

Carl also wants to purchase the same car. A private lender offers him \$20 000, which he uses to pay for the car. He repays the lender, in equal monthly payments of \$450, over 5 years.

Which person is better off and by how much? Justify with calculations.

solutions.latex:
Jason: the deposit is $10\%$ of \$20 000, which is \$2000, so the amount borrowed is \$18 000.
$$\begin{aligned} I &= 18\,000\times 8\%\times 5 \\ &= 7200 \end{aligned}$$
$$\text{Total}=2000+18\,000+7200=\$27\,200$$
Carl:
$$450\times 5\times 12=\$27\,000$$
Difference:
$$27\,200-27\,000=\$200$$
$$\therefore\ \text{Carl is better off by } \$200$$
criteria: Finds the difference, or equivalent merit
Finds Carl's total, or equivalent merit
Finds Jason's interest, or equivalent merit

parts.latex:
Omar has been keeping a bird count over the last four years in the school grounds.

In particular, he has been taking note of the Brown Treecreeper, a threatened species.

The number of sightings over the last four years are shown below.

\extable{308_q18_t1}

What was the greatest percentage decrease from one year to the next and how does this compare to the greatest percentage increase?

solutions.latex:
Percentage change from one year to the next, using $\dfrac{\text{change}}{\text{old value}} \times 100\%$:
$$\begin{aligned} 2019 \text{ to } 2020 &: \dfrac{28 - 32}{32} \times 100 = -12.5\% \\ 2020 \text{ to } 2021 &: \dfrac{27 - 28}{28} \times 100 \approx -3.6\% \\ 2021 \text{ to } 2022 &: \dfrac{31 - 27}{27} \times 100 \approx +14.8\% \end{aligned}$$
The greatest percentage decrease was $12.5\%$ (2019 to 2020).

The greatest percentage increase was about $14.8\%$ (2021 to 2022), which is greater than the greatest decrease by about $2.3$ percentage points.
criteria: Calculates the percentage changes correctly for at least one decrease and the increase, or equivalent merit
